title: Exercise 7A · Q13
summary: Split the figure into two triangles, find the missing lengths and add their areas.
alt: Exercise 7A · Q13: In the figure, ∠DGF = ∠EPF = 90°. Given that DE = 31 m, EF = 23 m, DG = 32 m and PF = 13 m, find the area of the figure.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: In the figure, **∠DGF = ∠EPF = 90°**, with **P** on **DF**. **DE = 31 m**, **EF = 23 m**, **DG = 32 m** and **PF = 13 m**. We have to find the **area of the figure DEFG**.

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔEPF, **∠P = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **EF**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides. We want a shorter side, so subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{EF^2} &= \role{legA}{PF^2} + \role{legB}{EP^2} \\ \role{legB}{EP^2} &= \role{hyp}{EF^2} - \role{legA}{PF^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and subtract
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{EF^2} &= \role{legA}{PF^2} + \role{legB}{EP^2} \\ \role{legB}{EP^2} &= \role{hyp}{EF^2} - \role{legA}{PF^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{23^2} - \role{legA}{13^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{529} - \role{legA}{169} \\ &= \role{legB}{360}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 360 is not a perfect square. Use a calculator and keep 4 significant figures — we need this value again.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{EF^2} &= \role{legA}{PF^2} + \role{legB}{EP^2} \\ \role{legB}{EP^2} &= \role{hyp}{EF^2} - \role{legA}{PF^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{23^2} - \role{legA}{13^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{529} - \role{legA}{169} \\ &= \role{legB}{360} \\ \role{legB}{EP} &= \sqrt{360} = 6\sqrt{10} = 18.97\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔEPD, **∠P = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **DE**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. (We know **EP² = 360** from the last step.) **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides. We want a shorter side, so subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{DE^2} &= \role{legA}{EP^2} + \role{legB}{DP^2} \\ \role{legB}{DP^2} &= \role{hyp}{DE^2} - \role{legA}{EP^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and subtract
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{DE^2} &= \role{legA}{EP^2} + \role{legB}{DP^2} \\ \role{legB}{DP^2} &= \role{hyp}{DE^2} - \role{legA}{EP^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{31^2} - \role{legA}{360} \\ &= \role{hyp}{961} - \role{legA}{360} \\ &= \role{legB}{601}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 601 is not a perfect square. Use a calculator and keep 4 significant figures — we need this value again.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{DE^2} &= \role{legA}{EP^2} + \role{legB}{DP^2} \\ \role{legB}{DP^2} &= \role{hyp}{DE^2} - \role{legA}{EP^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{31^2} - \role{legA}{360} \\ &= \role{hyp}{961} - \role{legA}{360} \\ &= \role{legB}{601} \\ \role{legB}{DP} &= \sqrt{601} = 24.52\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Find DF
steps.narration: **DF** is made of **DP** and **PF**.\[\begin{aligned}DF &= DP + PF \\ &= 24.52 + 13 \\ &= 37.52\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Area of ΔDEF
steps.narration: **EP** is the height of **ΔDEF** on the base **DF**.\[\begin{aligned}\text{Area of } \triangle DEF &= \tfrac{1}{2} \times EP \times DF \\ &= \tfrac{1}{2} \times 18.97 \times 37.52 \\ &= 355.9\ \text{m}^2\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔDGF, **∠G = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **DF**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides. We want a shorter side, so subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{DF^2} &= \role{legA}{DG^2} + \role{legB}{GF^2} \\ \role{legB}{GF^2} &= \role{hyp}{DF^2} - \role{legA}{DG^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and subtract
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{DF^2} &= \role{legA}{DG^2} + \role{legB}{GF^2} \\ \role{legB}{GF^2} &= \role{hyp}{DF^2} - \role{legA}{DG^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{37.52^2} - \role{legA}{32^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{1407.75} - \role{legA}{1024} \\ &= \role{legB}{383.75}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 383.75 is not a perfect square. Use a calculator and keep 4 significant figures — we need this value again.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{DF^2} &= \role{legA}{DG^2} + \role{legB}{GF^2} \\ \role{legB}{GF^2} &= \role{hyp}{DF^2} - \role{legA}{DG^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{37.52^2} - \role{legA}{32^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{1407.75} - \role{legA}{1024} \\ &= \role{legB}{383.75} \\ \role{legB}{GF} &= \sqrt{383.75} = 19.59\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Area of ΔDGF
steps.narration: **ΔDGF** is right-angled at **G**, so its area is half the product of **DG** and **GF**.\[\begin{aligned}\text{Area of } \triangle DGF &= \tfrac{1}{2} \times DG \times GF \\ &= \tfrac{1}{2} \times 32 \times 19.59 \\ &= 313.4\ \text{m}^2\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Total area
steps.narration: Add the two areas to get the area of the whole figure.\[\begin{aligned}\text{Area of DEFG} &= \text{Area of } \triangle DEF + \text{Area of } \triangle DGF \\ &= 355.9 + 313.4 \\ &= \role{ans}{669\ \text{m}^2}\ \text{(3 s.f.)}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Check EP²
challenges.prompt: In ΔEPF, EF = 23 m and PF = 13 m. Find **EP²**.

takeaways: To find the **area** of a figure, split it into triangles and add their areas.
Split the figure into right-angled triangles and solve them **one at a time**; each answer feeds the next triangle.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
